title: Terraform module change communication and subscriber workflow
content:
Summary:

This note captures a proposed lightweight workflow for communicating changes to Terraform modules that back Private deployments (VPC / on-prem customers). The goal: reduce surprise breakages for downstream consumers, make registry publishes predictable, and provide an automated subscriber notification path so customers and internal teams can plan upgrades.

Why we need this:
- We ship many tf modules that consumers instantiate in private deployments. Small incompatible changes have caused late-night rollbacks.
- Current publish is ad-hoc: author publishes tag, ops teams notice issues when upgrading stacks.
- We need a repeatable path that ties module versioning, changelogs, CI checks, and a subscriber notification channel.

Scope & audience:
- Applies to modules under repo: infra-modules/* that are consumed by private-deploy clusters and on-prem installers.
- Primary audience: module authors, SRE/Platform, Solutions Eng (customer-facing), and downstream integrators.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Enforced semantic versioning policy for modules (major.minor.patch semantics mapped to breaking, additive, and bugfix changes).
2) Pre-publish checklist and automated tests that must pass before a registry promotion.
3) A lightweight subscriber registry (email/Slack + optional webhook) where teams subscribe to specific modules and receive structured notices.
4) Standard deprecation window for fields and resources, with a migration helper included in module README.

Proposed workflow (end-to-end):
A) Author iteration (dev branch / PR)
- Author opens PR against infra-modules/<module>. Include: summary of change, proposed semver bump, migration notes, and a short smoke plan.
- PR template must have a required field: downstream-impact (none / additive / breaking). If 'breaking', author must add an upgrade plan and a compatibility test.
- Required checks run in CI: fmt/lint, terraform init/validate, unit-ish plan against a canonical test fixture, and a canary apply in a disposable GCP/AWS account (5–15m job).

B) Review & acceptance
- Module reviewers (owner + 1) confirm semver classification. For ambiguous cases, default to safer classification (major).
- If breaking: require explicit CHANGELOG entry and a migration helper script (optional terraform example workspace or docs) to be included in PR.

C) Pre-publish gating in CI
- On merge to main, CI generates an artifact containing: version tag, changelog excerpt (one-liner), migration notes, and test result matrix.
- CI must validate provider version constraints and run a quick static compatibility check across known consumer manifests (see consumers/fixtures).

D) Registry publish job
- A dedicated registry-publish pipeline (separate service account) picks up the artifact and publishes to the private module registry (internal registry path).
- The job should be idempotent and only publish packages with a signed tag (we use GPG or ephemeral signing via signing-service).
- Publish job writes an event to registry-event-bus with payload: module, old_version, new_version, changelog_excerpt, breaking=true/false, publish_time, author.

E) Subscriber notification & cadence
- Subscribers: teams can subscribe to modules via a small UI or by creating a subscription file in a repo (subscribers/<team>-subscriptions.yaml).
- On registry-event, a notification is sent: 1) Slack channel (#module-updates) with a short summary, 2) email digest to subscribers, 3) webhook to any registered endpoint.
- For breaking changes: notification includes recommended migration window (e.g., 90 days) and a call-to-action to open a support ticket if they need help.

F) Deprecation & rollback policy
- Deprecation window (recommended): 90 days for field/resource deprecation before removal in a next major.
- For emergency rollbacks, module owners can publish a hotfix patch version (x.y.z+1) or pin a compatibility fallback module that reintroduces the old behavior behind a feature flag.

Breaking-change checklist (must be present for any major bump):
- [ ] PR description: explicit "breaking" flag and rationale.
- [ ] Migration steps: step-by-step instructions, change to example usage, terraform plan output sample.
- [ ] Compatibility tests: smoke apply/plan against consumer fixtures + automation to detect resource renames.
- [ ] Changelog entry: human-friendly summary and machine-readable metadata.
- [ ] Registry event metadata filled: @author, jira/ticket, links to PR and acceptance logs.
- [ ] Subscriber notification drafted in a template (see below).

Pre-publish automation checks (CI):
- terraform fmt + validate (required)
- static resource rename detection (custom script)
- run 'terraform plan' against minimal fixture and ensure no resources are unintentionally recreated.
- run quick apply/destroy in ephemeral account (timeout 20m).
- compare outputs: if outputs removed/renamed, require explicit deprecation entries.

Subscriber notification template (machine-friendly):
- subject: MODULE_UPDATE: <module> v<old> -> v<new> [BREAKING]
- body: one-line summary, breaking: true/false, impact: short table (fields changed), migration-window: 90 days, link_to_changelog, link_to_migration_examples, contact (solutions-eng alias).

Consumer migration helper examples to include in module repo:
- examples/migrate-from-v1-to-v2/README.md with step-by-step terraform snippets.
- examples/lockfile-replace.sh: helper script to update module source references in downstream repos (grep/replace across manifests).
- examples/compatibility-test: tiny infra repo used by CI to validate the consumer surface area.

Rollout considerations for Private deployments / On-prem installers:
- Staged rollout: for on-prem installers, publish new module but do not update installer images automatically. Installer releases reference pinned module versions; update installer release notes with recommended installer version that picks up the module change.
- For VPC-managed fleet: recommend gradual rollout by tagging certain accounts/namespaces to receive upgrade scripts, monitor errors for 48–72 hours, then broader rollout.

Changelog format (machine friendly + human):
- Each tag includes a CHANGELOG.yaml at root with entries: date, version, type (breaking/additive/bugfix), summary, migration_link, jira_ticket. CI aggregates these into a release note.

Example small checklist for an author (TL;DR):
1) Determine semver bump.
2) Add CHANGELOG entry and migration example if needed.
3) Run CI tests locally (fmt/validate/plan fixtures).
4) Open PR, mark downstream-impact.
5) After review, merge -> publish pipeline sends notifications.

Edge cases / open questions (todo):
- How strict should we be about semver? Example: renaming an input that is unlikely to be used by customers but used in internal stacks — still major? Proposal: treat any public input/resource rename as major.
- Backwards-compatibility shims in modules: we can add internal translation layers but these increase maintenance cost. When to prefer shims vs major version? Need policy.
- Who signs off final publish for high-risk modules (networking, auth)? Suggest an "approver on call" list.
- What telemetry do we capture for breaking changes (how many downstreams tried to upgrade)? We should capture registry download counts and failed apply counts (if possible).

Notes to self / operational TODOs:
- Build registry-event-bus prototype (lambda / cloud function) to post Slack/email/webhook events.
- Add subscribers dir and sample subscription file to infra-modules repo.
- Implement static rename detector as a GH Action.
- Draft PR template changes and add required 'downstream-impact' field.

Next steps & owners:
- Priya: prototype registry-event-bus (2w) and sample webhook schema.
- Ethan: implement GH Action for rename detection (1w).
- Marta: update PR template and CHANGELOG.yaml schema (3d).
- Lin: draft subscriber onboarding doc for Solutions Eng (1w).

Appendix: quick example notification JSON (for webhook consumers):
{
  "module": "infra-modules/routing",
  "old_version": "1.4.2",
  "new_version": "2.0.0",
  "breaking": true,
  "migration_url": "https://git.internal/infra-modules/routing/examples/migrate-v1-to-v2",
  "publish_time": "2025-03-03T16:12:00Z"
}

(put that in examples/ as sample-webhook.json)

If you are reading: comments welcome — especially from Solutions Eng and SRE. This should be pragmatic, not bureaucratic. Start with minimal gating and evolve automation as pain points emerge.

-- Priya
